At nautical twilight, the sky is still fairly dark, and with clear conditions an ordinary observer should spot it readily.

Look toward the **west**, at roughly **azimuth 272°**—almost due west—and about halfway up the sky. It may be somewhat less conspicuous than under full darkness because dawn twilight is beginning, but it should still be obvious once you scan the correct area.
